title: I Want Bubbles
materials: bubbles, a wind-up toy, or another favorite repeatable activity
instructions: Play for a turn, then pause and model a short sentence such as 'I want bubbles.' Wait a few seconds and accept any closer attempt, then continue right away. Offer 3-5 natural openings during the activity.
success_criteria: The child attempts a three-to-four word request such as 'I want bubbles.'
make_easier: Accept a two-word version such as 'want bubbles' and expand it aloud once.
make_harder: Model a slightly fuller sentence such as 'I want more bubbles' without requiring it.
group_play_line: Each person takes a turn asking for the activity in their own words.
what_to_avoid: Do not withhold the activity while waiting for the full sentence.

title: Can I Play?
materials: a shared game, blocks, or any activity already underway
instructions: Start playing with something inviting. When the child shows interest, model 'Can I play?' and pause briefly. Welcome them in immediately after any attempt.
success_criteria: The child attempts a short question such as 'Can I play?' to join an activity.
make_easier: Accept 'play' or a gesture and expand it aloud.
make_harder: Model 'Can I play too?' without requiring the extra word.
group_play_line: Take turns asking to join each other's play.
what_to_avoid: Do not exclude the child from play to prompt the phrase.

title: Help Me Open
materials: a container with a lid, a zipped bag, a jar, or a wrapped snack
instructions: Offer something the child wants that needs opening. When they bring it to you, model 'Help me open.' Pause briefly, then open it right away.
success_criteria: The child attempts a three-word request naming the help needed, such as 'help me open.'
make_easier: Accept 'help' or 'open' and expand it aloud once.
make_harder: Model naming the object too, such as 'Help me open box.'
group_play_line: Another familiar person models the same request during shared play.
what_to_avoid: Do not create difficult or unsafe containers, or delay help to extend practice.

title: My Turn Please
materials: one favorite shared toy or a simple turn-taking game
instructions: Pass a favorite toy back and forth. Model 'My turn please' before you take it and pause before passing it so the child has an opening. Keep each turn short.
success_criteria: The child attempts a three-word turn-taking phrase such as 'my turn please.'
make_easier: Accept 'my turn' and expand it aloud without requiring repetition.
make_harder: Model 'Can I have a turn?' without making the longer form mandatory.
group_play_line: Two children use the same phrase while sharing one toy.
what_to_avoid: Do not withhold a turn until the phrase is produced correctly.

title: I Need a Break
materials: an ordinary play activity or daily routine
instructions: During an activity, model short sentences the child can use to pause or stop, such as 'I need a break' or 'All done now.' When the child communicates this, respond promptly so they learn the words work.
success_criteria: The child attempts a three-to-four word phrase to pause, stop, or finish.
make_easier: Accept 'break,' 'done,' or a gesture and model the fuller sentence once.
make_harder: Model 'I need a break please' without requiring the extra word.
group_play_line: Model respecting another person's request for a break during shared play.
what_to_avoid: Never ignore a clear request to stop in order to get a longer sentence.

title: Who Is Doing What
materials: toy animals, dolls, toy cars, or familiar play figures
instructions: Act out a simple scene with two familiar figures and model a short sentence naming who, the action, and the object, such as 'Dog eats the food' or 'Baby drinks milk.' Pause before acting so the child can try the sentence.
success_criteria: The child attempts a three-to-four word sentence combining a subject, an action, and an object.
make_easier: Use the same scene repeatedly and model the sentence before each action.
make_harder: Change one element and model the new sentence during the same play.
group_play_line: Let another person set up a scene and describe it in a short sentence.
what_to_avoid: Do not correct word order when the meaning is already clear.
